_comment: Single source of truth for the software apps shipped by this monorepo. Consumed by scripts/build_site.py (GitHub Pages landing page + deploy copy list) and scripts/publish_portfolio.py (portfolio cards + Obsidian notes). `summary` is the one-line portfolio-card copy (HTML-ready, keep it under ~120 visible characters so cards stay even); `description` is the full copy shown in the card's Details view and the Obsidian note (HTML-ready); `desc` is the short landing-page blurb. Optional `portfolio_order` overrides `order` for the portfolio card sequence only (the lowest values are the featured cards shown first); `portfolio: false` keeps an app off the portfolio without changing the landing page or notes. `links` are relative to the deployed site root (https://juw12.github.io/projects/<rel>). Extra fields `image_alt`, `project_id`, `label` (thumbnail aria-label) and `desc` reproduce the live markup verbatim. Card art (`image`, in the portfolio's assets/projects) must be house style: a 1600x1000 live-UI screenshot framed in the standard browser window on the dark accent gradient. Make it with `python scripts/portfolio_card.py <id>` (optional per-app `card` object: capture, frame_image, click, wait_ms, label, theme, accent, accent2) and never hand-draw, halftone or paste raw screenshots; publish_portfolio.py refuses cards that are missing, undersized or greyscale.

apps.description: Twin is an iPhone-ready investing and trading companion with a clean, professional design (1.5.1: new design system, line icons, dark and light themes) that tells you when a new version is ready and installs it in one tap. New in 1.15: the Twin desktop app for Windows and Mac — your own Twin server and app in one program, so real trading with Alpaca or Interactive Brokers needs no Python or terminal — and Add money: see your broker cash and buying power, follow a step-by-step deposit at your broker and get told when the money arrives (Twin never holds your money). From 1.14: updates inside the app — the installed app shows "Update ready" with what's new and updates in one tap (nothing reloads by surprise), and a Twin running on your own computer can update itself from the app: it downloads the published bundle, checks its SHA-256, backs up the whole Twin folder, keeps accounts and data, and restarts; Me shows the version with a Check for updates button. From 1.13: two wallets, one picture — move practice money between your US dollar portfolio and the Twin Indonesia rupiah wallet at the delayed mid rate minus a 0.5% practice spread; both ledgers update together (in one revision-checked request on your own server, or in this browser on the web demo), moved money counts as money put in so returns stay honest, and Portfolio and Me show both wallets and the combined total. From 1.12: the Twin Indonesia rupiah wallet shows on Home and Me, syncs to your Twin account on your own server (conflict-safe across devices), and Indonesian, crypto and gold headlines come from every feed through the server or refresh hourly on the web demo. From 1.11: Twin Indonesia, the rupiah side of Twin at twin/id/ — IDX stocks in 100-share lots with price steps and broker fees, US stocks at the shown USD/IDR rate, crypto and gold priced in rupiah, community rooms with Scam Shield, an Analyst Desk whose ideas are scored against real prices, and nine interactive lessons, with a separate rupiah practice wallet. From 1.10: a premium landing page and the premium look on every tab — glowing portfolio card on Invest, gradient academy and colourful course tiles on Learn, rounded Trade and News cards, and a big avatar header on Me. From 1.9: a premium dark design with a glowing balance hero, quick actions, swipeable cards and a Buy/Sell dock on every stock. From 1.8: big bold numbers, soft borderless cards, pill buttons, coloured ticker badges, a floating glass tab bar, charts that draw themselves in, count-up portfolio value and swipe-to-close sheets. New in 1.7: real-time prices from your own Interactive Brokers, Alpaca or Finnhub account with the source shown on every stock page (Yahoo stays the labelled, delayed fallback), a read-only IBKR gateway self-test, Qatar and Abu Dhabi holiday calendars, daily backups of your data and a safe updater. From 1.6: the web demo covers about 280 stocks and ETFs on 35+ exchanges plus 34 indices, refreshed hourly; market status follows real exchange calendars (holidays, early closes); FX rates refresh every minute with their time shown; and real orders can go through Interactive Brokers for world exchanges as well as Alpaca for US listings. From 1.5: TwinAgent, a free research team of five analysts (trend, SEC-filed fundamentals, risk, relevance-screened headlines, famous investors' 13Fs) that argue a bull and bear case from cited, dated evidence; a portfolio manager rates the stock and a risk gate built from your own limits sizes or blocks the idea. No AI subscription, the same evidence always gives the same report, future data is filtered out, and a walk-forward scorecard tests the price evidence over decades against buy-and-hold. Search stocks by company, ticker or country — Tokyo, Hong Kong, Jakarta, London, Frankfurt, Mumbai, Toronto, São Paulo, Sydney and more — with exchange, currency, market status and next holidays, ≈ USD price with the FX time and US-listing hints on every stock page. World markets shows market clocks, 34 indices, movers and a heatmap; practice trades in a separate $10,000 USD portfolio convert foreign prices at current FX rates, and totals can be shown in your home currency (25 currencies). Continue as guest or share a ?guest link; market, limit, stop, stop-limit and trailing orders with brackets, price alerts, scrub charts with SMA/EMA/RSI, portfolio X-ray with country and currency exposure, a bar-by-bar Replay Lab and 12 Twin Academy lessons. The local server searches any Yahoo Finance listing; the web demo uses an hourly snapshot of about 280 global stocks and ETFs. Optional real trading on the local server through your own Alpaca (US) or Interactive Brokers (world exchanges) account, with preview, confirm, caps and submission-time checks. Not financial advice.

apps.desc: One app for money and spreadsheets: a live, end-to-end encrypted shared budget with a money-personality plan, limit warnings and a portfolio, a Marketplace tab to buy, generate and sell budget plans, investing mixes and Excel / Google Sheets templates with instant checkout on the seller's own Midtrans, Xendit or Stripe; many currencies with daily rates, an investing quiz, tips and regional money news, and one encrypted account that syncs every device; asks your language and region first; free on Windows, Mac, Android, iPhone and the web
apps.summary: Shared budgets in any currency, synced on every device, plus a Marketplace for plans and templates. Free on every platform.
apps.description: Mint is one app with two halves. Budget is a budget you share like a Google Sheet, with an interface built only for money: a 30-second setup turns take-home pay into needs / wants / savings / investing envelopes, an optional 2-minute quiz assigns one of six money personalities, a live sheet with cell-level merging, warnings at 80%, over the limit or when your pace will overspend (including when someone else's edit tips a category), goals and an investing portfolio with drift and rebalancing. Sharing is local-first and end-to-end encrypted (AES-GCM, key in the link fragment) over ntfy.sh or a self-hostable stdlib relay, with no account. Templates is a live marketplace for Excel / Google Sheets templates: describe a sheet in English or Bahasa Indonesia and Mint AI designs it, tweak it with words (“add column Supplier”), export a real .xlsx with live formulas and a dashboard, then sell it — buyers pay the seller directly through the seller's own Midtrans, Xendit or Stripe checkout (QRIS, e-wallets, VA, cards) or a payment link, with coupons, tracked affiliate commissions, seller insights and Web Push notifications, on a Cloudflare Workers + SQLite Durable Object backend. Since 3.2, expenses, income and holdings can be in any currency and are converted to the budget's currency with daily exchange rates (the original amount is kept); Invest adds a 12-question quiz, personal tips and regional money news; the template studio lives inside Mint as a Marketplace tab where you can also sell your own budget plan or investing mix (shares of income only, never real amounts) and buyers see prices in their own currency; and one Mint account keeps budgets in sync on every device, encrypted on the device before upload (PBKDF2 + AES-GCM, with a recovery code). The first time it opens, Mint asks for a language (English, Bahasa Indonesia, 简体中文 or Español) and a region, and the region sets the currency of new budgets and templates. Both halves share one install, one icon, one light / dark / system theme and that one language (Templates is in English and Bahasa Indonesia), and update themselves in place. Free as a Windows and Mac desktop app, an Android app, an iPhone home-screen app and on the web; the desktop and Android builds are opened and checked on their own systems before every release. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step.
